utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry for the slight delay, but as you can see, we have to deal with the residue from another case. Before we turn to you, Mr. Knoops, could we have a short discussion on some scheduling matters. This afternoon, we have -- Mr. Knoops will make his opening submission on behalf of Mr. Stanisic. Then there's Dr. Tarabar for the Defence; and for the Prosecution, Dr. Smalc.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Now, I understand that Dr. Offermans is not available for Thursday. In any event, as it has turned out, Thursday is not a good day. Dr. Boomgaard.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. He arrives back in the country and would be available all day the 25th, but not before that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He had initially indicated the 19th, scheduled for the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I look on that with disfavour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We can't go beyond the 25th. We shouldn't. So I'm setting the 25th for Dr. Offermans and Dr. Boomgaard. That's a Tuesday, in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So it's on to you now, Mr. Knoops, to make your opening submission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. May I first please introduce to the Honourable Trial Chamber my learned friend Mr. Wayne Jordash. He is just appointed as co-counsel in this case and this will be his first appearance in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we are glad to have you, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honours, first of all, we thank you for giving the accused the opportunity to address you at this oral hearing. The Defence will address several topics to further elaborate on the motion for provisional release and the reply motion. We'll first address the presumption of innocence, in view of the Prosecutor's anticipation of a life sentence. Secondly, the principle of a fair trial and the principle of effective participation in combination with fitness to stand trial. And we will close with the issue of the guarantees. And we will incorporate also several remarks made by the OTP investigators. Mr. President, the presumption of innocence, as set out in Article 21, section 3 of the Statute of your Honourable Court not only applies from the moment a person is formally charged, thereby becoming an accused, but it also applies during pre-trial investigations. It is also envisaged the notion that the investigating authorities must also investigate in favour of the suspect. I'll point you to the recent textbook of Antonio Cassese at page 390, International Criminal Law. One of the consequences of this principle is that a defendant has the right to be held innocent until proven guilty and accordingly, should be granted fair chance to defend himself. Now, the question is: Is Mr. Stanisic to be considered according to the allegations which suggest he is a war criminal, or is he to be judged for the purpose of this bail application according to the evidence that suggests that, in the first place, he was ejected from the hospital by the regime in April 2000 due to his opposition to the Kosovo policy. See also Exhibit 22 of the motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Three --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just point out we are in open session. I believe Mr. Knoops had asked for Rule 70 protection on that particular --

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We are actually in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: According to my schedule it was the whole afternoon in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You didn't ask for it, so we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: This is a matter then that should be taken in private session. We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And the portion that you just mentioned will be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
